pages.text: "The door won't open!" Little brother Mumu pushed the mill door with his wings. Snow had piled outside all night. "I'll open it! I want to step in snow!" Another thump.
Big sister Dodo waddled over. "Let's push together." Mumu planted both wings on the door and shook his head. "No, I'll open it alone!"
Heave! Heave! Three pushes, and the door didn't budge. Only three wing marks remained. Mumu dropped onto the floury floor.
Dad came over wearing his straw hat. "If it's hard alone, you can ask to do it together." Dad looked at Dodo. "Push together, open the door! Maybe it will slide open?"
Mumu hesitated, then looked at Dodo. "...Will you push with me?" She quickly stood beside him. "Of course!" Side by side, they planted their wings on the door.
"One, two, three! Push together, open the door!" Heave! The door creaked open, and snow spilled through the gap. Cold wind blew in, fluttering Mumu's neck scarf.
Outside was a white yard. Mumu set his first foot in the snow. A duck footprint. Beside it, Dodo's footprint too. Two trails went out side by side.
"Alone, it wouldn't budge. Together, it slid open!" Mumu flicked his tail once. Dodo and Mumu slapped wings. Clap!

That evening, by a heavy sack, Mumu tapped the place beside him. "One, if it's hard, ask to do it together! Two, stand side by side! Three, push on one, two, three! Dodo, let's push together!" he said first.
Dad hugged both against his broad body. "Our two doorkeepers!" Something that won't work alone slides into place with two. Holding Dodo's wing, Mumu called, "Push together, open the door!"
